_comment: Analytics and data engineering. The thing that makes this environment different is that the expensive mistakes are often read-shaped rather than delete-shaped: a query against the wrong warehouse, or a copy of a table that should never have left. Copy to your project root as .blastradius.json and gitignore it.

rules.why: Destructive write against a warehouse. These tables are usually rebuilt from pipelines that take hours, and a dropped table can break every dashboard downstream of it.
Restoring a dump overwrites every table it contains. Confirm the target host and take a fresh dump first, because a restore aimed at the wrong environment is not recoverable by re-running it.
Moving what looks like personal data off its system of record. This is a compliance question before it is a technical one, and it is not something a backup undoes.
Making storage publicly readable. Once an object has been public, assume it was fetched, because crawlers are faster than you are.
Backfills and clears re-run history. On a wide date range this can cost real money and flood downstream consumers with duplicate events.
